value: A professional, scientific diagram in the style of a top-tier conference such as KDD, designed as a flat 2D vector academic figure with a clean white background, strict grid alignment, high-contrast readable text placeholders, and no 3D shadows, no photorealistic effects, no decorative metaphors, and no non-academic illustrative objects. Section 1 (Left): depict the input as a compact multivariate time-series block labeled $X \in \mathbb{R}^{T \times d}$, using a rounded horizontal rectangle with 2–3 thin internal sparkline traces to indicate temporal signals, followed immediately by a clearly separated preprocessing module labeled Instance Normalization, emphasizing that normalization is the mandatory first step in the main pipeline. Section 2 (Left-Middle): show an input-organization module labeled Channel-independent Patching, with an ordered array of small patch rectangles and a subtle side annotation for Sliding Window, conveying that each channel is treated independently while the same network is shared across channels; attach a restrained support branch for Multi-scale Patch Sizes using 2–3 parallel auxiliary tracks in muted gray-green with placeholder labels such as $s_1, s_2, \ldots$, clearly subordinate to the main flow rather than competing with it. Section 3 (Middle): from a single neat split node, expand symmetrically into two horizontally aligned scientific branches with shared-parameter semantics, the upper branch labeled Patch-wise Attention and the lower branch labeled In-patch Attention, both rendered as abstract attention blocks with consistent geometry, subtle internal line patterns, and a centered Shared Weights marker between them; the upper branch should represent dependencies across patches, while the lower branch should represent dependencies within each patch, and both must appear as two views of the same input rather than two unrelated encoders. Section 4 (Middle-Right): place explicit Upsampling Alignment modules on both branches at the same x-position, then output two aligned latent feature capsules labeled $N$ and $P$; if multi-scale enhancement is visualized, indicate that branchwise outputs are aggregated after alignment using a small Aggregate or Sum node, but do not introduce any ungrounded decoder, memory bank, negative sample pool, or reconstruction path. Section 5 (Right-Middle): route the aligned representations $N$ and $P$ into a central comparison node labeled Symmetric Discrepancy or KL-based Discrepancy, visually balanced with equal-length incoming arrows from both branches, making it clear that discrepancy is computed only after alignment; above the main pipeline, add a lighter training-only band with dashed purple connectors leading to a module labeled Symmetric KL Loss, annotated with $L\{P, N; X\}$ and Stop-gradient / Async Optimization, ensuring that this training path is visually weaker than the inference path and never merged into the final prediction route. Section 6 (Right): continue the solid main inference flow from the discrepancy node to a restrained anomaly output module labeled Anomaly Score, highlighted only with a controlled brick-red accent, then to a small diamond decision node labeled Threshold $\delta$, and finally to a clean output box labeled Predicted Label $Y_i \in \{0,1\}$; optionally place a compact side note indicating point-wise anomaly scoring, but keep the core chain as discrepancy to score to threshold to label. Use a disciplined conference figure palette dominated by low-saturation deep blue and blue-gray for core modules, muted gray-green for multi-scale support branches, soft purple for training-only loss paths, brick red only for anomaly-related emphasis, dark neutral text, light gray dividers, and pale gray grouping containers. Organize the full composition into clearly separated horizontal containers for Input & Preprocessing, Input Organization, Dual-view Representation Learning, Alignment & Scoring, plus an upper Training-only Band; keep all modules strictly aligned to a grid, with orthogonal or gently bent connectors, minimal line crossings, and balanced spacing between parallel branches. If a legend is included, place a small compact legend in the lower-right corner explaining main inference flow, training-only dashed supervision, multi-scale support branch, anomaly-related highlight, and shared-parameter dual branches. The final figure must emphasize the closed scientific logic of one input generating two complementary attention-based views whose aligned representation discrepancy drives both the training objective and the anomaly detection criterion, while preserving a concise, publication-ready, flat vector style suitable for a top-tier machine learning paper.
